chunks: Hariz narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

I asked him about the People of the Dhimma (covenant), what is upon them by which their blood and wealth are secured? He said: The land tax (Kharaj). If the Jizya is taken from their heads, then there is no claim on their lands; and if it is taken from their lands, then there is no claim on their heads.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Islamic rule)
key_terms.الجِزْيَةُ: The head tax paid by non-Muslims

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between Jizya and Kharaj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling to clarify the mutual exclusivity of Jizya (head tax) and Kharaj (land tax), ensuring that a Dhimmi is not doubly burdened for the same security guarantee. This distinction highlights the jurisprudential principle that fiscal obligations are tied to specific categories of wealth or status rather than cumulative liabilities, reflecting the practical administration of early Islamic states.
